review_notes: I read the whole file and the surrounding definitions it uses (eval_linearChange, dualMatrix_inv, standardHighest_apply). The only substantial repeated proof machinery I found is in standardHighest_upper_fixed and standardHighest_lower_orbit. Both unfold standardRepresentation through the dual and the inverse of dualMatrix, apply standardHighest_apply, rewrite with eval_linearChange and dualMatrix_inv, and then compute the evaluation point as the first column of the matrix. The pairs highestCoefficientMap_lower_intertwines / highestCoefficientMap_upper_intertwines and lower_eq_transvection / upper_eq_transvection are similar but differ enough, or are short enough, that factoring them out would not clearly pay off. My proposed lemma has not been compiled. The `simp` closing steps in its two uses may need small adjustments.

findings.problem: Both proofs redo the same reduction. standardRepresentation g applied to standardHighest is unfolded to standardHighest (homogeneousRepresentation (dualMatrix g⁻¹) f). They then use standardHighest_apply, linearChange, eval_linearChange and dualMatrix_inv, and finish with a hand-built `hrow` showing that the evaluation point is the first column of the group element. The two `hrow` computations (at lines 80-84 and 98-103) differ only in the matrix. The general fact is never stated, so the two proofs carry different copies of the same `change`/`rw` chain, including the same long `change` lines.
findings.proposed_change:
Add one lemma before standardHighest_upper_fixed:

lemma standardRepresentation_highest_apply (n : ℕ) (g : SL2 k)
    (f : MvPolynomial.homogeneousSubmodule (Fin 2) k n) :
    standardRepresentation k n g (standardHighest k n) f =
      MvPolynomial.eval (fun i => (g : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) k) i 0) f.val := by
  change standardHighest k n ((homogeneousRepresentation n (dualMatrix k g⁻¹)) f) = _
  rw [standardHighest_apply]
  change MvPolynomial.eval ![1,0] (linearChange (dualMatrix k g⁻¹) f.val) = _
  rw [eval_linearChange, dualMatrix_inv]
  congr 1
  funext i
  simp [Matrix.transpose_apply, Fin.sum_univ_two]

Proof sketch: this is the existing common prefix, with the final `funext` computing ∑ j, g i j * ![1,0] j = g i 0.

Use in standardHighest_upper_fixed: `ext f; rw [standardRepresentation_highest_apply, standardHighest_apply]; congr 1; funext i; fin_cases i <;> simp [unipotent]`. Here the first column of unipotent k t is ![1,0].

Use in standardHighest_lower_orbit: after `apply (binaryBasis k n).ext; intro i`, run `rw [standardRepresentation_highest_apply]` and `have hcol : (fun i => (lowerUnipotent k t : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) k) i 0) = ![1, t] := by funext i; fin_cases i <;> simp [lowerUnipotent]`, then `rw [hcol, binaryBasis_apply]` and keep the existing final two `simp` calls. Both uses keep their current hypotheses (k a field, n : ℕ, t : k) and need no new imports.
findings.benefit: The reduction from the representation action on the highest vector to evaluation at a column of g is proved once. The fact is a clear statement (the action on the highest-weight functional is evaluation at the first column), which also covers diagonal and general g. Each of the two lemmas shrinks to a column computation. Any change to how standardRepresentation or dualMatrix are defined only needs to be fixed in one proof instead of two parallel ones.
